Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: portrait 4:5 photograph for one Research & Innovation focus card on Masdar Al Hayat's Saudi food company website. This is an illustrative editorial image, not a claim to depict a specific real facility or employee.
Style across the series: authentic high-end documentary food-industry photography, natural warm-neutral daylight, subtle forest-green, cream, stainless-steel and muted copper environmental tones, realistic skin and material texture, believable hands and work practices, crisp subject with gentle background depth. Natural photographic contrast, no cinematic orange/teal grade, CGI gloss or oversaturated color.
Composition: portrait 4:5, visually clear main action in the upper and central 65% of the frame. Leave the bottom 30% quieter with simpler naturally darker surfaces so the website's overlaid white heading and paragraph remain legible. The subject must still be understandable in a small portrait card. No text, charts, graphics, floating icons, captions or watermarks. No visible brand names or logos, no invented Fonte packaging. Do not write the card title into the picture.
Scene: Consumer & Market Insight / Understanding people and markets. A candid real Saudi supermarket bread aisle. A female market researcher in a modest sage-green business outfit and hijab listens attentively to a woman shopper in a simple abaya, who indicates her choice between packaged loaf sizes on an accessible shelf. A shopping basket with ordinary groceries rests naturally nearby. The researcher holds a small plain notebook at waist height with no readable writing. Show their genuine conversation and attention to consumer choices, not a posed handshake or promotional photoshoot. Only two people, physically credible shelf layout, neutral unbranded bread packaging, no legible store signs. Medium editorial shot focused on listening and observation, actual shopper context.

A Saudi food technologist and a baker in immaculate plain white food-safe coats and hairnets thoughtfully compare the softness and texture of a few small trial bread loaves and tortilla samples. One person gently opens a small bread sample to inspect its crumb while the other examines a tortilla edge. Bowls of oats, whole wheat flour and measured ingredients, a small digital kitchen scale and simple utensils sit naturally on a clean workbench. No packaged retail products, no labels, no lab flasks, no charts or dramatic machinery. Close medium three-quarter composition with attentive expressions, hands and food samples sharply visible in the upper/middle frame. Realistic hygienic culinary R&D, warm natural side light.

Scene: Packaging & Convenience / Packs designed for real life. A thoughtful hands-on food packaging development table in a clean modern food-company workspace. A packaging specialist's clean hands compare a compact individually sealed pastry portion with a resealable transparent tortilla pouch and a clear bread bag containing a small intact loaf. Show opening/resealing, sizing and practical portion formats; the hands align a clear pouch closure precisely, showing how convenience is evaluated. Include a small open reusable lunchbox at the far side as a believable everyday-use cue, and a restrained stack of plain cream packaging samples. All prototypes transparent or plain with absolutely no printed brand, product text or invented Fonte identity. Physically plausible clear film seals and plastic reflections, real food visible inside, no machinery wall or retail display. Slightly elevated close-up focused on hands, closures and varied pack formats, quiet uncluttered bench in lower third.

A realistic food quality technician in a plain clean white coat, hairnet and properly worn disposable gloves checks the temperature of a small freshly produced loaf using a compact calibrated probe thermometer at a hygienic stainless-steel inspection bench. A second small sealed unbranded food sample and a simple scale are nearby. Focus on careful product verification and protection early in development, not medical science or a generic factory tour. Show the probe entering the loaf correctly, believable hands and posture, a clean bakery quality workspace softly out of focus behind. No readable numbers, interfaces, paperwork or labels. No Fonte/Masdar logos, no invented laboratory credentials, no production-line branding. Medium close shot of focused technician and inspection action, soft clean daylight with neutral whites.

In a real organized food-business warehouse dispatch workspace, a logistics/process specialist in a clean dark-green work shirt uses a handheld barcode scanner to scan an unbranded food carton while a colleague confirms the matching stock movement on a rugged tablet. The tablet is seen mainly from the back or a shallow oblique angle with no readable screen. Keep the scanning action, carton identification and collaboration unmistakable. A few orderly neutral cartons and a restrained rack recede into soft background depth. Do not make this merely a wide warehouse image: show the useful digital tool being used in the foreground, connected to a real physical workflow. No charts, holograms, fake analytics dashboards, floating data graphics, invented labels, logos or brand names. Realistic handheld scanner, unobtrusive small barcode without readable text, natural practical work environment.

Scene: Open Innovation & Partnerships / Growing through shared knowledge. An authentic collaborative food-development workshop in a modern Saudi meeting room connected to a test kitchen. Three professionals — a Saudi commercial/customer representative in a white thobe, a female food technologist in a modest professional hijab outfit, and a supplier specialist in a plain light shirt — discuss ingredient and plain packaging prototypes together at a table. They actively exchange ideas: one points to a small grain sample and a test bread loaf while the others listen and contribute. Warm natural expressions, candid working interaction rather than posed handshake. A few small food samples, transparent unbranded prototype pouches, oats and simple notebooks on the table; do not crowd it. No laptops facing the camera, charts, signs, legible writing or logos. No branded packaged products that would risk changing an actual product identity. Frame all three people and the shared experiment in upper/middle area, calm darker tabletop below.

hanini.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied transparent cutout photograph of the existing Hanini Brioche retail package.
The user is happy with EVERYTHING about this image except that the visible bread looks sliced. Make ONE extremely localized change: replace the visible stack of bread slices INSIDE THE CLEAR PLASTIC WINDOW with ONE intact, unsliced, whole brioche loaf occupying exactly the same space. Erase the repeated horizontal slice seams and divisions in the exposed bread. Give it a continuous natural golden-brown loaf crust and soft baked texture, with the same existing food color and the same exterior silhouette. Keep the loaf fully contained within the existing bag and fully visible wherever the bag is transparent. Do not add a loose loaf outside the packaging or a bread slice illustration. The entire packaged loaf and bag must remain in frame.
STRICT LOCK: preserve the original exact bag geometry, height/width proportions, orientation and camera angle, burgundy tied top, closure, plastic wrinkles and reflections, maroon/gold/black/white geometric heritage artwork, every Fonte logo, brand text, NEW label, no-added-sugar roundel, source-of-fibre badge, Arabic and English lettering, typefaces, nutrition marks, net-weight marks and label positions. All printed areas and the exterior of the package are locked and must remain visually identical to the input. Do not rewrite, redraw, improve, redesign or reinterpret any packaging graphics. Only the real food behind the transparent window may change. In particular, do not create new text or replace the existing Fonte mark. The user explicitly said do not change anything else.
Maintain the original transparent background and alpha cutout, with no cast ground shadow, tabletop, new background, margins, captions, watermark, people or added objects. Match the original slim portrait canvas and native crop; do not stretch or squat the bag. Output a high-quality photorealistic cutout with natural food detail, never CGI.
This is the FRONT VIEW. The bread-only change is restricted to the exposed window in the upper half, behind the existing printed NEW, Fonte logo and no-added-sugar badge. Keep all that printed foreground artwork exactly as it is. Keep the lower gold Hanini label and its surrounding heritage pattern completely unchanged.
hanini.note: Only the front asset is replaced. Original side and back views retained.
